prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1163; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports a head injury diagnosed as a concussion and says they are not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy file and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. Witness statements on file describe the accident the same way the claimant did.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement both confirm the collision happened as described. The damage visible on the vehicle matches the impact reported.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant by phone. They gave the same account of the collision that was recorded at intake, with no changes in the sequence of events.

Entry 6: Inspected the vehicle and found no earlier damage in the affected areas. Nothing in the file suggests any damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 7: Asked the claimant about any prior head or neck injuries. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the information provided so far.

Entry 8: Medical records show treatment for the concussion followed a usual course, with visits tapering off as the claimant improved. Whether the injury came from this crash has not yet been established and will need further medical review.

Entry 9: Second call with the claimant to check on symptoms and recovery. They repeated the same account of the accident and said they are feeling better.

Entry 10: Requested updated treatment notes and a physician's statement to clarify the link between the collision and the diagnosis. Awaiting response.

Entry 11: Reviewed the full file. Liability and vehicle damage are consistent with the reported loss. The bodily injury portion stays open pending the medical review.
